question.problem: Consider the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R$ defined by $f(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{3}.$ What is the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a scalar-valued function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ with respect to a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ is the row vector

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{1\times n}.
$$

In our case, the function 

- acts on a vector $x\in {R}^{2},$ and

- outputs a scalar $f(x)\in R$ defined by 

$$
f(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{3}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{3})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1} & 3{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{1\times 2}.\end{aligned}
$$
